If you only remember one thing today, make it this. The E U A I Act is now being enforced. But the hardest parts of it just slid seventeen months to the right. The pressure this year is on transparency, not on high risk certification.

Section one. The rulebook went live, and then moved.

From August second, the European Commission's A I Office, working with national authorities, began actually enforcing the A I Act. New transparency requirements applied the same day.

But the timeline shifted underneath it. Standalone high risk systems, the ones listed in Annex Three, recruitment tools, credit scoring, education, law enforcement, border control, critical infrastructure, now face full compliance on December second, twenty twenty-seven. Not August this year. That is a seventeen month extension. A I embedded in products already covered by European product safety law, medical devices, machinery, toys, moves further still, to August twenty twenty-eight. And Article Five now bans A I systems built to generate non consensual intimate imagery, effective December second of this year.

Why it matters. Anyone who built a twenty twenty-six compliance story around the high risk deadline now has a messaging problem and eighteen extra months, because transparency obligations are what's actually live today.

Section two. A flaw that crossed all three big labs at once.

Researchers disclosed a flaw in how Open A I, Anthropic and Google each carried hidden model reasoning between A P I calls. It let weaker models recover the internal reasoning of stronger ones. Worse, it pulled secrets out of session logs, including A P I keys and passwords.

Why it matters. This is a rare shared architecture failure, not one vendor's mistake, which makes we patched it a much harder story to tell on your own.

Section three. Model news, and the money behind it.

X A I shipped Grok four point six on August twelfth. It matches G P T five point six Sol Max on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, sixty-one points each, at the same price as Grok four point five. G P T five point six Luna dropped eighty percent in price and became the Chat G P T free default. Gemini crossed one billion monthly active users on August eleventh. And Qwen shipped a new twenty-seven billion parameter model on the fourteenth.

On the business side. Anthropic reported second quarter revenue of ten point nine billion dollars, up a hundred and thirty percent, and its first operating profit, five hundred and fifty-nine million dollars, roughly two years ahead of its own plan. Open A I's S one filing is expected any day, with a September listing target, two billion dollars a month in revenue, and a projected fourteen billion dollar loss for this year.

Why it matters. Capability gaps are closing while prices collapse. The competitive story is shifting from who is smartest to who can afford to keep giving it away.

Section four. From your Reads. China's week, via Recode China A I.

The China A I Weekly Digest tracked two hundred and sixty-three stories. Three stood out.

DeepSeek shipped V four Pro and open sourced an agentic coding tool called DeepSeek Harness. It's M I T licensed and explicitly aimed at Anthropic's Claude Code. Then DeepSeek raised A P I prices by as much as eleven times. Reviews were mixed. Strong on coding and cybersecurity, underwhelming elsewhere.

Unitree's Shanghai I P O was oversubscribed thousands of times over, with retail odds around one in fifty-five hundred. Meanwhile, South China Morning Post reports AgiBot has already passed Unitree as the world's top humanoid vendor by first half shipments.

And Meta unwound its two billion dollar Manus deal after Chinese regulators blocked the acquisition. Tencent is now the agent startup's top shareholder, and Manus is independent again. Revenue reportedly soared through the whole mess.

Also in that digest. Tencent's A I capital spending hit fifty-two point eight billion yuan in the quarter, and free cash flow reportedly went negative for the first time. Memory chip maker C X M T overtook Tencent as China's most valuable company. And Uber and Pony point A I announced plans for more than two thousand robotaxis across Europe.

Why it matters. The competition has moved from benchmarks to agent harnesses and distribution. And Chinese firms are now scaling outward, not just upward.

Section five. Chips. That's the top of the news. Your full briefing is in the recording.
